subject: Estimating regression effects in multiple group SEM when some groups have no variance in the predictor

messages.author: d3700dd3210d01b2
messages.subject: Estimating regression effects in multiple group SEM when some groups have no variance in the predictor
parts:
Hi lavaan group,

I am looking at associations between education and cognition (a latent variable called "cog" with indicators "v1"-"v22") using multiple group SEM. The four groups are those with:

1) 0 years of education (no education)
2) 1-5 years of education (incomplete elementary)
3) 6 years of education (elementary)
4) 7+ years of education (beyond elementary)

I structured the model so intercepts, estimated separately by group, capture group differences in cognition and I created a years of education variable "yrs_edu" to predict cognition and capture within group differences in cognition by education in groups 2 and 4.

One issue I have is that groups 1 and 3 all have the same level of education (no variance in years of education). Is it possible to specify that education should only predict cognition in groups 2 and 4?

One potential solution is imputing random numbers for years of education in groups 1 and 3 (those with no variance in years of education) and then fixing the years of education parameter estimates to 0 for those groups (using the syntax below). However, I end up getting the error below stating that the wrong number of arguments are entered. The error message shows that I only put 2 arguments, however, 4 were included in my syntax to match the number of groups (cog ~ (0,b,0,b)*yrs_edu).

Error in lavaanify(model = FLAT, constraints = constraints, varTable = lavdata@ov,  :
  lavaan ERROR: wrong number of arguments in modifier (b,b) of element cog~yrs_edu

Any potential solutions to include regressions in certain groups when other groups have no variance in the variable?

Thank you in advance!

mod3<- '

# latent variables
cog =~ NA*v1 + v2 + v3 + v4 + v5 + v6 + v7 + v8 + v9 + v10 + v11 + v12 + v13 + v14 + v15 + v16 + v17 + v18 + v19 + v20 + v21 + v22

# means
cog ~ c(0,NA,NA,NA)*1

# variances
cog~~(1,NA,NA,NA)*cog

# regressions
cog ~ (0,b,0,b)*yrs_edu
'

# estimating the model
mod3.fit <- cfa(mod3, data=cogdata, std.lv=TRUE, estimator="WLSMV", missing="pairwise", ordered=c("v2", "v3", "v9", "v10", "v11", "v14", "v15", "v16", "v17", "v18", "v19", "v20", "v21", "v22"), parameterization="theta", group="edgroup", group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "thresholds"))
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Estimating regression effects in multiple group SEM when some groups have no variance in the predictor
parts: One issue I have is that groups 1 and 3 all have the same level of education (no variance in years of education). Is it possible to specify that education should only predict cognition in groups 2 and 4?

Fixing the slope to zero in groups 1 and 3 won't work because the sample covariance matrix is NPD when there is zero variance.

Instead, you can use the block-style syntax to specify separate models per group.  Then you can just leave the variable out of groups 1 and 3 but include it in groups 2 and 4.

There is an example of such a model here:

https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/uyq3h0wXh6g
